nnn - Supercharge your productivity!

`nnn` (_n³_) is a full-featured terminal file manager. It's tiny, nearly 0-config and incredibly fast. It is designed to be unobtrusive with smart workflows to match the trains of thought. `nnn` can analyze disk usage, batch rename, launch apps and pick files. The plugin repository has tons of plugins to extend the capabilities further e.g. live previews, (un)mount disks, find & list, file/dir diff, upload files. Runs on the Pi, Termux (Android), Linux, macOS, BSD, Haiku, Cygwin, WSL, across DEs or a strictly CLI env. ## Features - Quality - Privacy-aware (no unconfirmed user data collection) - POSIX-compliant - Highly optimized code - Frugal - Typically needs less than 3.5MB resident memory - Works with 8 colors (and xterm 256 colors) - Disk-IO sensitive (few disk reads and writes) - No FPU usage (all integer maths, even for file size) - Minimizes screen refresh with fast line redraws - Tiny binary (typically around 100KB) - 1-column mode for smaller terminals and form factors - Portable - Language-agnostic plugins - Static binary available (no need to install) - Minimal library deps, easy to compile - No config file, minimal config with sensible defaults - Plugin to backup configuration - Widely available on many packagers - Touch enabled, handheld-friendly shortcuts - Unicode support - Modes - Light (default), detail - Disk usage analyzer (block/apparent) - File picker - Navigation - Filter with automatic dir entry on unique match - *Type-to-nav* (turbo navigation/always filter) mode - Jump to an entry with visible relative offset - Contexts (_aka_ tabs/workspaces) with custom colors - Sessions, bookmarks, mark and visit a dir - Remote mounts (needs `sshfs`, `rclone`) - Familiar shortcuts (arrows, ~, -, @), quick look-up - `cd` on quit (*easy* shell integration) - Proceed to next file on file open and selection - Search - Instant filtering with *search-as-you-type* - Fuzzy, regex and string (default) filters - Subtree search plugin to open or edit files - Sort - Ordered pure numeric names by default (visit `/proc`) - Case-insensitive version (_aka_ natural) sort - By name, access/change/mod (default) time, size, extn - Reverse sort - Directory-specific ordering - Mimes - Preview hovered files in FIFO-based previewer - Open with desktop opener or specify a custom opener - File-specific colors (or minimal _dirs in context color_) - Icons and Emojis support (customize and compile-in) - Plugin for image, video and audio thumbnails - Create, list, extract (to), mount (FUSE based) archives - Option to open all text files in `$EDITOR` - Convenience - Detailed file stats and mime information - Run plugins and custom commands with hotkeys - FreeDesktop compliant trash utility integration - Cross-dir file/all/range selection - Create (with parents), rename, duplicate files and dirs - Create new file or directory (tree) on startup - Batch renamer for selection or dir - List input stream of file paths from stdin or plugin - Copy (as), move (as), delete, archive, link selection - Easily copy, move paths in system clipboard to current dir - Dir updates, notification on `cp`, `mv`, `rm` completion - Copy file paths to system clipboard on select - Launch apps, run commands, spawn a shell, toggle exe - Access context paths/files at prompt or spawned shell - Lock terminal after configurable idle timeout - Capture and show output of a program in help screen - Basic support for screen readers and braille displays ## Usage Don't memorize! Arrows, /, q suffice. Tab creates and/or cycles contexts. ? lists shortcuts. For detailed usage instructions, command-line options, and configuration information, please refer to the man page (`man nnn`) or visit the project Wiki. ## Installation `nnn` is available on many package managers. Install it using your distribution's package manager, or download a pre-built static binary. Common installation methods: - **Arch Linux**: `pacman -S nnn` - **Debian/Ubuntu**: `apt install nnn` - **Fedora**: `dnf install nnn` - **macOS (Homebrew)**: `brew install nnn` - **FreeBSD**: `pkg install nnn` For more installation options and detailed instructions, visit the project Wiki. ## License BSD 2-Clause License Copyright © 2016-2026 Arun Prakash Jana and contributors See LICENSE file for full license text.

.Dd Feb 14, 2026
.Dt NNN 1
.Os
.Sh NAME
.Nm nnn
.Nd The unorthodox terminal file manager.
.Sh SYNOPSIS
.Nm
.Op Ar -aAcCdDeEfgHJKnQrRSuUVxz0h
.Op Ar -b key
.Op Ar -F val
.Op Ar -l val
.Op Ar -p file
.Op Ar -P key
.Op Ar -s name
.Op Ar -t secs
.Op Ar -T key
.Op Ar PATH
.Sh DESCRIPTION
.Nm
.Pq Nnn's Not Noice
is a performance-optimized, feature-packed terminal file manager
with seamless desktop integration, simplified navigation,
.Em type-to-nav
mode with dir auto-enter, disk usage analyzer mode, bookmarks,
contexts, application launcher, familiar navigation shortcuts,
subshell spawning and much more. It remains a simple and
efficient file manager that stays out of your way.
.Pp
.Nm
opens the current working directory if
.Ar PATH
is not specified. If

.Ar PATH
is considered a path to a regular file and
.Nm

import subprocess, time, os, sys, shlex
def tmux(args):
    subprocess.run(["tmux"]+args, check=False)
def capture(session="test"):
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t",session,"-p","-e"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout
def capture_plain(session="test"):
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t",session,"-p"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout

def start(cmd, session="test", w=80,h=24):
    tmux(["kill-session","-t",session])
    # ensure clean env: use env?

def keys(*k, session="test", wait=0.4):
    for key in k:
        tmux(["send-keys","-t",session, key])

def kill(session="test"):

if __name__=="__main__":

from harness import *
def fresh(opts=""):
    start(f"TERM=xterm-256color /workspace/executable {opts} /tmp/testdir; echo EXIT:$?; sleep 20")
def do(label,fn):
    fn(); c=cap(); print(">>",label); print("\n".join([l for l in c.splitlines() if l.strip()]))
# Quit flows
for name,seq in [
 ("q single context", [lambda: lit("q")]),
 ("Q", [lambda: lit("Q")]),
 ("Ctrl-Q", [lambda: key("C-q")]),
 ("Ctrl-G QuitCD", [lambda: key("C-g")]),
 ("Esc then y", [lambda: key("Escape"), lambda: lit("y")]),
 ("Esc then n", [lambda: key("Escape"), lambda: lit("n")]),
 ("Esc Esc", [lambda: key("Escape"), lambda: key("Escape")]),
 ("Esc then Enter", [lambda: key("Escape"), lambda: key("Enter")]),

REF='/tmp/reference_executable'; OURS='/workspace/executable'
def run(exe,args,inp=b'',env_extra={}):

    env.update(env_extra)
    r=subprocess.run([exe]+args,input=inp,capture_output=True,timeout=3,env=env)
    return r.returncode,r.stdout,r.stderr.replace(exe.encode(),b'EXE')
cases=[]
for args in [['-h'],['-V'],['-K'],['-x'],['-y'],['--help'],['-'],['--'],['-F'],['-F','2'],['-F','-1'],['-F','x'],['-l'],['-b'],['-b','x'],['-T','x'],['-hV'],['-Vh'],['-K','-h'],['-F','2','-h'],['-z','-h'],['extra1','extra2'],['/nope_xyz/'],['-p'],['-s'],['-t','abc']]:

for opts in ['h','V','K','Z','-H','x','Hd','1','?']:
    cases.append(([],{'NNN_OPTS':opts},b''))
for inp in [b'',b'\n',b'/tmp\n']:
    cases.append(([],{},inp))
for env in [{'NNN_BMS':'x'},{'NNN_PLUG':'x'},{'NNN_FCOLORS':'0'},{'NNN_ARCHIVE':'['}]:

    a=(a[0],a[1],a[2].replace(REF.encode(),b'EXE')); b=(b[0],b[1],b[2].replace(OURS.encode(),b'EXE'))
    if a!=b:

import subprocess,time,os,sys
def tmux(a):return subprocess.run(['tmux']+a,capture_output=True,text=True)
def cap(esc=False,hist=False):
 a=['capture-pane','-t','test','-p']
 if esc:a.append('-e')
 if hist:a+=['-S','-300','-E','-']
 return tmux(a).stdout
def run(exe,cmd_tmpl,steps):
 subprocess.run(['bash','-c','rm -rf /tmp/cmphome /tmp/cmp_ops && mkdir -p /tmp/cmphome/.config /tmp/cmp_ops/sub && printf hello >/tmp/cmp_ops/a.txt && printf world >/tmp/cmp_ops/b.log && touch -d "2020-01-02 03:04" /tmp/cmp_ops/a.txt /tmp/cmp_ops/sub'])
 tmux(['kill-session','-t','test'])
 cmd=cmd_tmpl.replace('{EXE}',exe)
 tmux(['new-session','-d','-s','test','-x','80','-y','24',f"HOME=/tmp/cmphome XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/cmphome/.config TERM=xterm-256color {cmd}; echo EXIT:$?; sleep 20"])
 time.sleep(.7)
 out=[cap()]
 for label,kind,val in steps:
  if kind=='lit':tmux(['send-keys','-t','test','-l',val])
  elif kind=='key':tmux(['send-keys','-t','test',val])
  time.sleep(.5);out.append(cap())
 hist=cap(hist=True)
 tmux(['kill-session','-t','test'])
 # normalize list tmp names
 import re
 out=[re.sub(r'/tmp/nnn[A-Za-z0-9]{6}','/tmp/nnnXXX',x) for x in out]
 hist=re.sub(r'/tmp/nnn[A-Za-z0-9]{6}','/tmp/nnnXXX',hist)
 return out,hist

def scen(name,cmd,steps=[]):
 a,ah=run('/tmp/reference_executable',cmd,steps); b,bh=run('/workspace/executable',cmd,steps)
 ok=a==b
 print(('PASS ' if ok else 'FAIL ')+name)
 if not ok:
  for i,(x,y) in enumerate(zip(a,b)):
   if x!=y:print(' step',i,'\nref:\n',x,'\nours:\n',y)
 if ah!=bh and name.startswith('help'):
  print('hist diff\nref',ah,'\nours',bh)

import subprocess,os
def run(env):
 e=os.environ.copy(); e.update(env); e['TERM']='xterm'
 r=subprocess.run(['/tmp/reference_executable','/tmp'],input=b'',capture_output=True,env=e,timeout=3)

void open_with_opener(const char *path)
{
    if (gcfg.editor_text && !gcfg.cli_opener && is_text_file(path)) {
        edit_file(path, false);
        return;
    }
    const char *prog = G.opener;
    if (!prog) {
        if (!find_in_path("xdg-open")) return;
        prog = "xdg-open";
    }
    int n = 0; char **w = split_words(prog, &n);
    /* A custom opener is a single program (no arguments); the desktop
     * opener fallback is used when the value does not resolve. */
    bool custom_ok = n == 1 && find_in_path(w[0]);
    freev(w, n);
    if (G.opener && !custom_ok) return;
    if (gcfg.cli_opener) run_words_fg(prog, path, false);
    else run_detached_words(prog, path);
}

static bool g_autoadvance = false;
static bool op_open_entry(Entry *e, bool enter_key)
{
    if (!e) return false;
    char *path = entry_path(e);
    if (e->is_dir) {
        char *absd = abs_path(path);
        free(path);
        return change_dir_abs(absd, NULL);
    }
    if (gcfg.picker_file) {
        if (sel_index(path) < 0) { sel_add(path); sel_write_file(); }
        g_picker_pick_and_exit = true;
        free(path);
        return true;
    }
    if (S_ISREG(e->mode) && e->size == 0) {
        set_msg("empty! edit/open with");
        free(path);
        return false;
    }
    if (gcfg.open_enter_only && !enter_key) { free(path); return false; }
    if (!e->is_dir && is_archive_name(e->name)) {
        op_archive_open(e, path);
        free(path);
        return true;
    }
    open_with_opener(path);
    free(path);
    return true;
}

/* Open with a user typed program ('o'). */
static char *read_line_native(const char *prompt)
{
    suspend_curses();
#ifdef HAVE_READLINE
    char *line = readline(prompt);
    if (line && *line) add_history(line);
    resume_curses();
    return line;
#else
    fputs(prompt, stdout); fflush(stdout);

    while (r > 0 && (line[r-1] == '\n' || line[r-1] == '\r')) line[--r] = 0;
    return line;
#endif
}

/* Read one logical key.  An Escape promptly followed by another byte is
 * reported as an Alt combination. */
static int get_key(int *mod_escape_pending)
{
    (void)mod_escape_pending;
    if (pending_key >= 0) { int pk = pending_key; pending_key = -1; return pk; }
    int k = read_key_raw();
    if (k != ESC_KEY) return k;
    /* peek for a following byte */
    timeout(100);
    int k2 = read_key_raw();
    timeout(100);
    if (k2 == ERR) return ESC_KEY;
    if (k2 == ESC_KEY) return KEY_ALT_ESC;
    if (k2 == '\n' || k2 == '\r' || k2 == KEY_ENTER) return KEY_ALT_ENTER;
    if (k2 == KEY_BACKSPACE) return KEY_ALT_BASE + 127;
    if (k2 >= 0 && k2 < KEY_MIN) return KEY_ALT_BASE + k2;
    /* function key after ESC: push it back and report plain ESC */
    unget_wch((wchar_t)k2);
    return ESC_KEY;
}
static bool is_alt_key(int k, int ch)
{
    return k == KEY_ALT_BASE + ch;
}
